correctness.rationale: With alpha=2/p, log sinh(alpha t) concavity between alpha=1 and alpha=2 gives the claimed derivative sign; the sharp mixed coefficient is reached at equal positive inputs. The simplex inball, tested against the negative radial direction, gives max_i |q-v_i|² at least r²+R²+2rR/(d-1); the coefficients match exactly at p_d. For p>2 one instead uses l_p <= l_2 on the two scalar blocks. For |t|>=a the nearest apex vertical term is at most |t|^p; for |t|<a it is at most R^p. These cover the endpoint and all scales. Below threshold the explicit s satisfies s>lambda_d and s²>q_*, giving r_f<a<R and strict opposite inequalities at a base vertex (base distances <=s<1; both apex distances >1); the mixed/Euclidean Lipschitz bound supplies the claimed positive-volume open ball. All-base ties force q=g where a nearer apex beats the bases. In the horizontal plane on the facet-centroid-to-centroid segment, writing q-g=-u(v_i-g) for 0<u<=1/(d-1), the excluded squared distance minus a retained squared distance is 2uR²d/(d-1)>0. The retained distances cross the common apex distance a before u reaches zero. Downward closure and direct alternating summation on present apex indices give the exact nerve and sign. The frozen 456 checks use floating point and discrete samples; they were inspected, not rerun, and are not used for the universal result.
